# Knowledge Pages — lifecycle-typed sibling directories

Templates for the four typed directories added beside the existing
anti-hallucination knowledge cards (`agents/knowledge/<source>.md`,
[`knowledge-card.md`](knowledge-card.md)). **Existing cards stay untouched
by this template** — sibling addition, not a migration.

## The four directories

| Directory | Lifecycle stage | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `agents/knowledge/sessions/` | Episodic | What happened — consolidated session learnings, one file per topic or date |
| `agents/knowledge/concepts/` | Semantic | What is true — project facts: coding standards, module structure, API shapes, domain terms |
| `agents/knowledge/procedures/` | Procedural | How to — step-by-step knowledge on the way to becoming a skill (`skill-candidates.md` lives here) |
| `agents/knowledge/decisions/` | Decision record | Small decisions not big enough for a full ADR |

`agents/knowledge/INDEX.md` catalogs all five surfaces (cards + the four
directories), one line per page — generated by
`src/scripts/generate_knowledge_index.ts`. **Retrieval protocol: index
first, `grep` keywords second, read the specific file third.** Never
enumerate every knowledge file directly — no search infrastructure by
design.

## Storage location IS the sharing policy

Personal, cross-project knowledge → the ADR-100 user-global store
(`~/.event4u/agent-config/knowledge/`, via `knowledge_global_cli.ts`) —
never these project-local directories. Team knowledge → here, in the
consumer repo, so the whole team benefits via git. Promotion to global
requires cross-project evidence via the existing manual promotion path —
never automatic.

**Enforced at commit time.** A pre-commit gate
(`src/scripts/check_knowledge_sharing.ts`) refuses a commit staging a
`visibility: private` page under `agents/knowledge/` (belongs in the
global store) or a gitignored `agents/memory/intake/` file staged by
accident. Warns — never blocks — on 5+ new knowledge files in one
commit, for a second look.

## Entry micro-schema — `date + what + why`

Every entry (especially in `sessions/`) states, at minimum:

```markdown
- 2026-07-05: <what happened / was learned> — <why it matters>
```

Keep entries short; longer explanation goes in the page body below the
entry list, not stuffed into one line.

## Page frontmatter — optional, warn-linted only (v1)

None of these fields are mandatory in v1 (schema-as-contract deferred
until real team usage data exists). When present, warn-linted for shape
only:

```yaml
---
type: concept            # concept | procedure | session | decision
scope: project            # user | project | global
visibility: team           # private | project | team
review_after: "YYYY-MM-DD" # optional scheduled re-check date
contested: []              # append-only array — see "Contested entries" below
---
```

## Contested entries — never silently resolved

A live contradiction between documented and observed reality gets an
**append-only** `contested:` entry, never a silent rewrite:

```yaml
contested:
  - timestamp: "2026-07-15T14:23:11Z"
    trigger: context_stale
    evidence: "profile.test.ts:45 expected {success, payload}"
    session: "<session id or chat-history pointer>"
```

Resolution is always human — via the `team-knowledge:consolidate` gate,
or an isolated, this-turn-approved fix commit. ≥2 unresolved `contested`
entries on one page → flagged by the knowledge lint for consolidation
attention.

## Page size budget

Keep pages ≤ 200 lines. Split by sub-topic before that limit — a
too-broad page defeats index-first scanning just as much as too many
tiny pages do.
